Trello was decommissioned agency-wide effective **September 1, 2025**; after that date, existing Trello boards and cards will no longer be accessible [references/source-207.md]. Anyone needing to retain Trello content must export it beforehand, using JSON format (not CSV) to preserve full board content including comments [references/source-207.md]. GSA IT has not designated a single official replacement, though alternatives are suggested [references/source-207.md].

Autonomous AI agents are explicitly **not allowed** to contribute to ripgrep. The project requires a human in the loop who understands any AI-assisted work, and pull requests that appear to violate this policy will be closed, potentially without notice [references/source-002.md]. While using AI/LLMs as coding tools is otherwise welcomed—maintainers and contributors remain fully responsible for any published code [references/source-002.md]—all such contributions must adhere to this AI Policy, and any that don't will be closed [references/source-004.md].

Ripgrep can search compressed files by using the `-z`/`--search-zip` flag, which invokes its built-in decompression support; for formats not covered by that built-in support, ripgrep offers a mechanism via its FAQ entry "How do I search compressed files?", though the passages provided only confirm the existence of this FAQ topic without detailing the specific fallback mechanism [concepts/faq.md]. The evidence does not include the actual FAQ answer text describing how unsupported formats are handled (e.g., any external decompressor hook), so I cannot state that mechanism with certainty from the given passages.

To search inside compressed files, use ripgrep's `-z/--search-zip` flag, which automatically searches files compressed in gzip, bzip2, xz, lzma, lz4, Brotli, or Zstd formats; this requires the corresponding decompression binaries (`gzip`, `bzip2`, `xz`, `lz4`, `brotli`, `zstd`) to be installed, since ripgrep decompresses by shelling out to these external processes [references/source-005.md][references/source-007.md]. For formats or decompression needs beyond what `-z` supports, ripgrep offers arbitrary input preprocessing filters, which can be used for things like PDF text extraction, less-common decompression, decrypting, or automatic encoding detection [references/source-007.md].
